newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria takes on power project left by World Bank.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria takes on power project left by World Bank.

text.p: State-run National Electric Power Authority (NEPA) said on Monday it had taken over funding of transmission and distribution projects in the country after international creditors pulled out.

"NEPA is now funding the transmission and distribution projects entirely after the World Bank and the European Investment Bank pulled out," Hamzat Ibrahim, managing director of the state utility told reporters in Lagos.

The two credit agencies were financing a $700 million Lagos distribution expansion project approved in the early 1980s, to improve power supply to Lagos, the nation's commercial hub of six million where black outs are common.
Ibrahim declined to say why the lending agencies pulled out from the project but other NEPA sources said it had to do with Nigeria's political situation.
The nation plunged into turmoil in 1993 when the army annulled a presidential vote to restore democracy. Western nations have since shunned Nigeria and cut development aid.
The World Bank and the European Investment Bank had expended about $250 million mainly on construction of sub-stations in Lagos before withdrawing from the project in 1995.
"We are now financing the downstream component of the project which involves installing distribution equipment," Ibrahim said.
NEPA would spend 700 million naira ($8.24 million) to put three of the completed sub-stations into use before the end of this year, he added.
